description: Create the dedicated RELEASE CI chain .github/workflows/android-release.yml (separate from android-debug.yml), plus the human-facing stable-signing documentation and the signature-continuity test protocol. The release workflow is workflow_dispatch ONLY, builds in Consumer Cloud Mode (SCENEVIBE_ENABLE_LAN_DEV=false, SCENEVIBE_CLOUD_ORIGIN=https://interface-scenevibe-3wxg.vercel.app), runs assembleRelease to produce the UNSIGNED non-debuggable release APK, then apksigner-signs it with the four GitHub repo secrets. CRITICAL DIFFERENCE from debug workflow: if the four signing secrets are absent, the release workflow must FAIL EXPLICITLY with a clear error (not a silent soft pass). It must NOT auto-publish to Play Store and must NOT auto-create a GitHub tag/release. Depends on FEAT-002 (release variant must exist).
steps: Create .github/workflows/android-release.yml. Trigger: `on: workflow_dispatch:` ONLY (no push, no pull_request). permissions: contents: read. runs-on: ubuntu-latest.

Steps: actions/checkout@v4; actions/setup-java@v4 (temurin 17); android-actions/setup-android@v4; gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4 with gradle-version 8.9 (match debug workflow); `sdkmanager "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0"`.

FIRST job step after setup: an explicit secret-presence GATE that FAILS the workflow when any of the four secrets is empty. Compute SIGNING_ENABLED at job env level exactly like android-debug.yml (secrets compared != '' — secrets are not usable in step-level if:). Then a step: `if [ "$SIGNING_ENABLED" != "true" ]; then echo '::error::Release signing secrets are not configured. All four of SCENEVIBE_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 / _KEYSTORE_PASSWORD / _KEY_ALIAS / _KEY_PASSWORD must be set as GitHub repository secrets. Unlike the debug workflow, a release MUST NOT be produced unsigned.'; exit 1; fi`. This step must run BEFORE build so the workflow fails fast and clearly.
Run the Python boundary tests and :app:testDebugUnitTest first (preserve existing quality gates) so a release never ships from a red tree.

Build the Consumer Cloud Mode release: step env `SCENEVIBE_ENABLE_LAN_DEV: "false"` and `SCENEVIBE_CLOUD_ORIGIN: https://interface-scenevibe-3wxg.vercel.app`; run `gradle :app:assembleRelease --stacktrace`. The output is app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release-unsigned.apk.
Validate non-debuggable in CI: run aapt dump badging on the unsigned release APK and FAIL if an `application-debuggable` flag is present (grep -q 'application-debuggable' && exit 1).

Decode keystore into RUNNER_TEMP from SCENEVIBE_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 (printf '%s' | base64 -d), exactly like the debug workflow pattern, and NEVER echo its contents. Then apksigner sign a copy of the unsigned release APK into RUNNER_TEMP/scenevibe-tv-companion-release.apk using --ks + env-provided --ks-pass / --ks-key-alias / --key-pass (env: references, never inline). Then zipalign check is implicit via apksigner; run `apksigner verify --print-certs` and save stdout to a file release-apksigner-verify.txt.

Produce the required release artifacts into a staging dir: (1) the signed release APK; (2) release-apksigner-verify.txt (apksigner verify --print-certs output); (3) APK SHA-256 via `sha256sum` into apk-sha256.txt; (4) signing certificate SHA-256 fingerprint — extract from `apksigner verify --print-certs` output (the 'Signer #1 certificate SHA-256 digest:' line) into cert-sha256.txt; (5) a secret-free metadata file release-metadata.json containing EXACTLY: versionName, versionCode, applicationId, commit SHA (github.sha), apkSha256, certificateSha256, cloudOrigin, targetSdk (35), compileSdk (35). Pull versionName/versionCode/applicationId from the APK via aapt dump badging (do not hardcode). Assert the metadata file contains NO secret (no password, no keystore, no base64 key).

Upload a single artifact named `scenevibe-tv-companion-release` containing the signed APK + verify output + sha256 files + metadata json. if-no-files-found: error. Do NOT upload the keystore or any secret. Always-discard the decoded keystore and the staged signed apk copy in RUNNER_TEMP in an `if: always()` final step.
Add NO `gh release create`, NO tag push, NO Play Store publish step anywhere.

Create docs/stable-signing.md: a concise, exact, Windows/PowerShell human procedure covering: (a) generate the stable key ONCE locally with keytool (give the exact keytool -genkeypair command with -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -validity large, using PLACEHOLDER alias and NO real passwords — explicitly instruct the human to choose their own strong passwords and never share them); (b) store the .jks off-repo and back it up (never in the repo, never in a ticket/PR/log); (c) produce Base64 for GitHub with PowerShell `[Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('scenevibe-stable.jks'))`; (d) fill the four GitHub repository secrets (Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions) naming each; (e) keep the reference certificate SHA-256 fingerprint (keytool -list -v) off-repo as the continuity anchor; (f) verify a future APK is signed by the SAME key via `apksigner verify --print-certs app.apk` and comparing the SHA-256 digest to the reference. Add a clear architecture note distinguishing: our sideload/qualification signing key (what these four secrets are) vs a Google Play upload key vs Google Play App Signing — state that THIS cycle uses a self-managed stable key for sideload/qualification APKs, that Play upload key / Play App Signing is a SEPARATE future decision not configured here, and do not invent Play Store policy. No real password value anywhere in the doc.

Create docs/signature-continuity-protocol.md: the exact later-on-Sony protocol — install first stable APK with `adb install scenevibe-...-release.apk`, then upgrade with `adb install -r <next-stable>.apk`, success criterion = upgrade completes WITHOUT INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE, plus how to compare the two APKs' signing certs beforehand with `apksigner verify --print-certs` (identical SHA-256 digest = same key = compatible upgrade). State explicitly this is a HUMAN/PHYSICAL step not performed by CI or by this cycle; provide the elements to compare certificates in advance.

Do not run the signed-release path locally (secrets absent). Validate locally only: that the workflow YAML is well-formed, and that assembleRelease + aapt non-debuggable check succeed (reuse FEAT-002 commands). The signing portion is CI-ONLY and secret-gated.
acceptance_criteria: .github/workflows/android-release.yml exists, is workflow_dispatch-only, builds Consumer Cloud Mode (ENABLE_LAN_DEV=false, the exact Vercel origin), runs assembleRelease, and FAILS EXPLICITLY with a clear ::error:: and exit 1 when the four signing secrets are absent.

The workflow apksigner-signs the unsigned non-debuggable release APK and uploads artifact `scenevibe-tv-companion-release` containing: signed APK, apksigner verify --print-certs output, APK SHA-256, certificate SHA-256 fingerprint, and a secret-free release-metadata.json with exactly versionName, versionCode, applicationId, commit SHA, apkSha256, certificateSha256, cloudOrigin, targetSdk, compileSdk.
The workflow contains NO Play Store publish, NO auto tag, NO auto GitHub release, and never echoes/uploads keystore or password material; the decoded keystore is discarded in an always() step.

docs/stable-signing.md gives the exact Windows/PowerShell generate-once / store-off-repo / base64 / four-secrets / keep-fingerprint / verify-future-APK procedure with NO real passwords and a clear sideload-key vs Play-upload-key vs Play-App-Signing distinction.

docs/signature-continuity-protocol.md documents the adb install then adb install -r upgrade test (success = no INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE) and the pre-comparison of signing certs, explicitly marked HUMAN/PHYSICAL and not performed here.
assembleRelease + non-debuggable validation pass locally; signing path documented as CI-only/secret-gated.
verification: python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/android-release.yml')); print('release workflow YAML OK')"
/opt/android-sdk/build-tools/35.0.0/aapt dump badging app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release-unsigned.apk | grep -i debuggable || echo 'NON-DEBUGGABLE OK'
findings: Created .github/workflows/android-release.yml (workflow_dispatch ONLY, permissions contents:read, ubuntu-latest). Mirrors the android-debug.yml safe signing patterns (job-level SIGNING_ENABLED boolean because secrets are not usable in step-level if:; keystore decoded into RUNNER_TEMP via printf | base64 -d; env: references for passwords/alias, never inline; apksigner verify --print-certs; always() discard step) but adds a FAIL-FAST gate: when SIGNING_ENABLED != 'true' the workflow emits ::error:: and exit 1 before any build, so a release is never produced unsigned. Build is Consumer Cloud Mode (SCENEVIBE_ENABLE_LAN_DEV=false, SCENEVIBE_CLOUD_ORIGIN=https://interface-scenevibe-3wxg.vercel.app) via gradle :app:assembleRelease; gradle pinned 8.9 (assembleRelease runs lintVital which only works under 8.9). Quality gates run first (python boundary tests + :app:testDebugUnitTest). Non-debuggable validated with aapt dump badging grep -q application-debuggable. Artifact scenevibe-tv-companion-release contains: signed APK, release-apksigner-verify.txt, apk-sha256.txt, cert-sha256.txt (extracted from the 'certificate SHA-256 digest:' line), and release-metadata.json with EXACTLY versionName/versionCode/applicationId/commitSha/apkSha256/certificateSha256/cloudOrigin/targetSdk/compileSdk. versionName/versionCode/applicationId are pulled from the APK via aapt (not hardcoded). A defensive grep asserts the metadata JSON has no secret material. NO Play Store publish, NO tag, NO gh release. Replaced an indentation-fragile heredoc with printf to build the JSON reliably inside the YAML block scalar. Created docs/stable-signing.md (Windows/PowerShell keytool -genkeypair RSA 4096 -validity 10000 with PLACEHOLDER alias and NO real passwords; store .jks off-repo + backup; [Convert]::ToBase64String base64; the four GitHub secrets; keep keytool -list -v SHA256 fingerprint off-repo; verify future APK via apksigner verify --print-certs; architecture note distinguishing sideload/qualification key vs Play upload key vs Play App Signing, both Play paths marked separate future decisions not configured here) and docs/signature-continuity-protocol.md (adb install then adb install -r, success = no INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE, pre-compare certs via apksigner verify --print-certs digests, explicitly marked HUMAN/PHYSICAL not run by CI or this cycle). LOCAL VALIDATION (all green): release workflow YAML parses with PyYAML; gradle 8.9 :app:assembleRelease BUILD SUCCESSFUL (incl. lintVitalRelease) emitting app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release-unsigned.apk; aapt dump badging shows NO application-debuggable; aapt badging parsing yields applicationId com.scenevibe.tvcompanionpoc / versionCode 11 / versionName 0.8.1-tv-recovery; simulated metadata JSON is valid and secret-free; cert-digest sed extraction verified against a sample apksigner line. Signing path is CI-ONLY/secret-gated (the four secrets are absent in the sandbox); no key/password/keystore was generated, hardcoded, committed, or logged. tests/__pycache__/ left untracked (not committed). REVIEW v1 FOLLOW-UP (2026-10-01, iteration 1): addressed both findings in the 2026-10-01-210734-review.md. Issue 1 (CONFIRMED, blocking) the 'Validate release APK is NOT debuggable' step was fail-open (no set -e, `if` read grep's pipeline exit code, so a failed aapt would feed empty input to grep and the step would falsely print NON-DEBUGGABLE OK). Rewrote it to fail CLOSED: added `set -euo pipefail`, an explicit `[ -f "$UNSIGNED_APK" ]` existence assertion, and capture of `BADGING="$("$AAPT" dump badging ...)"` with a non-empty check (proving aapt actually ran and produced output) BEFORE grepping for application-debuggable. Issue 2 (possible, non-blocking) added a comment pinning the `certificate SHA-256 digest:` grep label to build-tools 35.0.0 (the version pinned via sdkmanager), noting the existing empty-digest hard-fail catches any future label change. Only .github/workflows/android-release.yml changed; no signing logic, secret-gating, artifact set, or metadata fields altered; no product/manifest/test/interdicted file touched. VERIFIED: (a) PyYAML parses the workflow (OK); (b) built the real APK with gradle 8.9 :app:assembleRelease (BUILD SUCCESSFUL incl. lintVitalRelease); simulated the new validation block against the real app-release-unsigned.apk -> prints NON-DEBUGGABLE OK (OK path preserved), and against a nonexistent path -> emits ::error:: and exits 1 (fail-closed confirmed; old code would have printed NON-DEBUGGABLE OK). No stray __pycache__ left; working tree clean apart from the intended workflow change.
